w10_T4_002810: A bakery had 208 buns on its racks and baked 32 more. Every bun was cut into 2 halves for a sandwich order, and the halves were divided equally into 5 boxes, one for each delivery van. Maya drove one of the vans, and she ate 9 of the halves from her box on the road. Her colleague Theo ate more from his box than Maya did. The oven runs at 200 degrees. How many bun halves were left in Maya's box?
w10_T4_002813: Riverside School's Year 6 has 131 students, but 12 were absent on the day of the trip collection. Each student who was present handed in 5 dollars. The parents' association then tripled the amount collected, so the fund stood at triple what the students had paid. The coach hire and museum tickets cost 1762 dollars, which came out of the fund. Afterwards one parent donated 35 dollars, and another parent also gave 35 dollars. How many dollars are left in the trip fund?
w10_T4_002815: Omar's orchard had 215 apple trees, but 182 diseased trees were cut down. Each remaining tree yielded 5 crates of apples, and each crate weighed 5 kilograms. His neighbour Lena, whose harvest was smaller than Omar's, gave him 31 kilograms of her apples to sell with his. The cider mill paid 9 cents for every kilogram, and Omar recorded the payment in cents although a hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents did the mill pay Omar?
w10_T4_002816: A tour company had 173 passengers booked for the coast trip, and 37 more booked on the day. The passengers were divided equally among 3 coaches. Each passenger on the first coach paid 6 dollars for a lunch box, and the driver of that coach was also given 40 dollars in tips. Each coach has 80 seats, and the journey takes one hundred and fifty minutes, that is, two and a half hours. How many dollars did the first coach's driver collect in lunch money and tips altogether?
w10_T4_002820: In the morning Tessa picked 148 ripe tomatoes from her vines and then 73 more from the greenhouse, putting them all in one basket. She cut every tomato in the basket into 6 thick slices for the market stall's sandwich counter. In the afternoon 471 of the slices went into sandwiches. In the evening she diced every slice that was left into 8 small cubes for salsa, and her helper added 29 cubes of tomato from his own crop to the salsa bowl. How many cubes of tomato were in the salsa bowl?
w10_T4_002829: In the morning a bakery baked 125 baguettes and then 8 more for a late order, a job that took three hours, one hundred and eighty minutes. Each baguette was cut into 2 halves, and each half was sliced into 4 pieces for the party platters. In the afternoon 21 extra pieces from a spare loaf were added to the platters. In the evening the caterer topped every piece on the platters with 9 olives. How many olives were used?
w10_T4_002830: Through the morning and early afternoon Nadia's stationery shop sold 131 pens in each of 7 hours, four hundred and twenty minutes of trading in all. Later in the afternoon a school order added 72 pens, a second school added 80, and a walk-in customer bought 33 more. In the evening Nadia priced the day's sales at 6 dollars per pen. Her brother Karim's shop across the road took in less than Nadia's that day. Nadia's shop took in exactly that same daily amount on each of the 5 days it opened that week. How many dollars did Nadia's shop take in over the 5 days?
w10_T4_002831: Coach Ines ordered 108 tubes of tennis balls, with 6 balls in every tube, and also had 80 loose balls in the storeroom. During the club tournament 681 balls were used up and thrown away. Afterwards a visiting team returned 28 balls they had borrowed. Coach Ravi's club has fewer balls in its storeroom than Coach Ines's club. How many tennis balls does Coach Ines have now?
w10_T4_002843: A candle shop received 240 boxes, each holding 5 candles, in a delivery that took two hours to unpack, one hundred and twenty minutes. The owner added 51 candles left over from last season to the stock. During the festival she sold 945 candles. A customer then returned a dozen candles that were the wrong colour. How many candles does the shop have in stock now?
w10_T4_002845: In a puzzle game, Rita has 204 coins and earns 60 more by finishing a dozen levels. At the game shop she converts every coin into 8 gems, and then picks up 23 loose gems in a bonus room. Every gem is then traded for 9 sparks, and she finds 36 extra sparks in a treasure chest. Finally, each spark is worth 7 points on the leaderboard. Her friend Joel is below her on the leaderboard. How many points does Rita have?
w10_T4_002849: Dev collected 86 dollars in sponsorship for a charity walk that took him five hours, three hundred minutes. His uncle had promised to triple whatever he collected, and he did, so the fund stood at triple the original amount. Afterwards his aunt gave 36 dollars, his teacher gave 36 dollars, a neighbour gave 19 dollars, and his grandmother gave 38 dollars. Dev's sister Sana raised less than Dev. How many dollars did Dev raise in total?
w10_T4_002852: In the morning a pizzeria had 173 dough balls in the fridge; 107 were used for lunch pizzas and 25 had gone stale and were thrown out. In the afternoon the chef divided every remaining dough ball into 3 smaller balls for garlic knots, then mixed 64 fresh small balls and later 73 more, all going into the same tray. In the evening every small ball in the tray was baked and cut into 4 pieces for the tasting menu. How many pieces were there?
w10_T4_002853: Ravi's nursery had 47 empty pots. He sold 28 pots, received a delivery of 77 pots, and then dropped a tray and broke 21 pots. He filled every pot he had left with half a bag of compost and planted 4 seedlings in each pot. Each seedling gets 7 millilitres of water a day; Ravi measures in millilitres, though he knows a thousand millilitres make a litre. His colleague Sunita's seedlings use less water a day than Ravi's. How many millilitres of water do Ravi's seedlings need each day?
w10_T4_002854: In the morning the library's returns trolley held 160 books, and 21 more books were returned before ten o'clock. In the afternoon a dozen volunteers reshelved 37 books from the trolley. In the evening 63 books came back through the drop box, and 3 more were handed in at the desk just before closing. How many books were on the returns trolley at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_002855: Lena had 111 marbles in a jar that weighs 3 kilograms when full. She gave 51 marbles to the school raffle. She then divided the marbles she had left into 2 equal shares, one for herself and one for her brother Max. Her aunt gave Lena 7 more marbles, but she lost 7 marbles in the garden. Lena and Max now have the same number of marbles. How many marbles does Lena have now?
w10_T4_002856: A warehouse received 137 pallets, each stacked 3 layers high with 9 cartons in every layer. It shipped 1928 cartons to a supermarket chain. It then received 27 cartons back from a cancelled order and 58 cartons from a supplier. The warehouse is 40 metres long. Finally it shipped 292 cartons to a corner shop. How many cartons are in the warehouse now?
w10_T4_002862: Hana's phone plan started the month with 184 minutes. She bought a 57-minute top-up and then received a 23-minute loyalty bonus. The provider then credited her with 73 minutes by mistake, and later removed those 73 minutes when the error was found. Her father then transferred 65 minutes from his own plan to hers. Hana knows sixty minutes make an hour, but the plan counts in minutes. Her brother Jiro has fewer minutes on his plan than Hana. How many minutes does Hana have now?
w10_T4_002864: In the morning a fruit stand had 64 peaches and sold 51 of them. In the afternoon the farmer dropped off 4 more peaches, and 1 peach was found rotten and thrown away. In the evening the stallholder packed the remaining peaches equally into 4 bags and took one bag round to her neighbour, who added 26 peaches from her own tree to that bag. How many peaches were in the bag then?
w10_T4_002870: In the morning Pedro unpacked 140 boxes of mangoes, with 2 mangoes in every box, onto his market stall. By noon he had sold 136 mangoes. In the afternoon a farmer brought him 58 more mangoes. In the evening a restaurant bought every mango he had left at 9 pesos each and added a 34-peso tip. Pedro's neighbour Ana took in less from her stall than Pedro did in the evening. How many pesos did Pedro receive from the restaurant?
w10_T4_002871: Yara saved 92 dollars a week from her job for 4 weeks. She received 23 dollars for her birthday, spent 55 dollars on a jacket, earned 57 dollars babysitting, and then paid 163 dollars for a concert ticket. She keeps her account in dollars, though she knows a hundred cents make a dollar. Her friend Sami has less saved than Yara. How many dollars does Yara have saved now?
w10_T4_002872: Ken had 121 sticker sheets and bought 38 more. He then gave 141 sheets to his little sister Mia, who now has more sheets than Ken. Ken peeled all the stickers off his remaining sheets, 8 stickers per sheet, and sorted them into packs of 6 stickers. At the school fair he sold every pack for 9 cents. How many cents did Ken make at the fair?
w10_T4_002873: Farmer Bea has 22 dairy cows and buys 79 more at auction. Each cow gives 7 litres of milk a day, and she collects all the milk for 3 days into one tank. Her barn has 15 stalls. A neighbour then pours 6 litres of his own milk into the tank. Her rival Carl's tank holds less milk than Bea's. How many litres of milk are in Bea's tank?
w10_T4_002875: A charity shop had 104 winter coats on its rails and received 38 more in donations. It sold 69 coats in the first week and sent 71 coats to a homeless shelter. The shelter later sent 69 coats back because it had run out of space, and a school collected 16 more coats for the shop. The shop has 3 rooms. How many coats does the shop have now?
w10_T4_002876: A cinema's main screen has 7 rows of 70 seats. At an ordinary show, half of the seats are filled, and each person pays 5 dollars. The cinema runs 9 shows a week on that screen, and the season lasts 6 weeks. If every show in the season is an ordinary show, how many dollars does the screen take in over the season?
w10_T4_002879: In the morning a juice bar received 119 kilograms of oranges. In the afternoon two more deliveries brought 78 kilograms and 30 kilograms. In the evening a final crate added 60 kilograms; the bar weighs everything in kilograms, though it knows a thousand grams make a kilogram. Every kilogram of oranges is turned into juice that sells for 3 dollars. How many dollars will the day's oranges bring in?
